correctness.rationale: By the defining relations, a rotation image of a gives either a central map or a coset-type pair (u,v) with u odd. If the image of a is outside the rotation subgroup it has order four, so odd m is impossible; for 4|m the image of b would square to one and could not invert it. For m=2h with h odd there are exactly four choices of image of b for each outside image of a, generating Q8. For m≥3 automorphisms preserve the unique cyclic subgroup of order 2m. On coset maps the action sends v to rv+(1−u)s at fixed u. Translations reduce this to units acting modulo d=gcd(u−1,2m), giving the stated gcd labels and orbit sizes. On the quaternion-type fiber with a↦b, the stabilizer has s=0 or m according to r≡1 or 3 mod 4. For r≡3 the precomposition contributes the extra central factor a^m to the new image of b; this cancels the rotation swaps and exchanges the two coset choices. Thus two fixed choices and one pair yield sizes 2m,2m,4m. Central maps give the stated parity-dependent orbits. For m=2 a proper image is abelian and the domain abelianization has exponent two, ruling out order four; the three nonzero central characters are transitive and the 24 automorphisms give the five S4 classes. Interchanging the gcd-divisor sum with the sum over odd u gives the arithmetic total.
residual_risks: The replay samples parity and the small quaternion case; unrestricted completeness is supplied by the algebraic proof.

value.rationale: The uniform classification distinguishes maps of the same image order even when image-subgroup data or raw endomorphism counts cannot. It gives a complete exact invariant on a standard nonabelian family and explains precisely where quaternion-image maps escaping the characteristic cyclic subgroup occur, how the orbits split, and why Q8 requires separate treatment. These are useful classification facts beyond a small-group enumeration.
residual_risks: This is a single-endomorphism orbit classification for one family, not a classification of all metacyclic groups or tuples of maps.
